correctness.rationale: On K_N minus a perfect matching, three eigenvalues N-2, -2,0 give antipodal amplitude -1/2+(1/2-1/N)exp(2it)+(1/N)exp(-i(N-2)t). Its squared modulus satisfies a sum-of-three-nonnegative-terms deficit identity. For N=2m with odd m>=3, setting t=pi/2+eps reduces the lower bound to g_m(eps)=(m-1)sin^2(eps)+cos^2((m-1)eps). Differentiating gives -2(m-1)cos(m eps)sin((m-2)eps); all critical candidates and endpoints show min g_m=m sin^2(pi/(2m)), achieved at eps=+/-pi/(2m) where the discarded nonnegative term also vanishes. Hence exact global max cos^2(pi/N), equality at t=pi/2 +/- pi/N modulo pi. Independently formed adjacency matrices and diagonalized for N=6,10,14, reproducing optima 0.75, 0.904508497187..., 0.950484433951...; finite matrices merely verify the exact proof.
